newsitem.title: JAPAN: Dollar surges to 120 yen, highest in 47 months.
newsitem.headline: Dollar surges to 120 yen, highest in 47 months.

text.p: The dollar rocketed to 120 yen in Tokyo trading on Friday, its highest level in almost four years, after comments from Japanese officials that a weak yen poses no threat to the Japanese economy.
Brokers said the dollar hit 120 yen, its highest point since February 1993, after the comments unleashed a wave of dollar buying among banks.
"We do not see it (the weakness of the yen and a drop in stock prices) as stalling the economy," Masayuki Matsushima, director of the research department at Japan's central bank, told reporters.
He said that for now the weakness in the yen was working to help boost Japanese corporate profits by making Japanese exports more competitive.
The comments signalled an apparent shifting of gears by Japan's finance mandarins, who have been bemoaning the currency's steep decline since the start of the year.

The greenback rose as far as 120.15 yen before slipping back slightly to trade at around 119.75 yen. Foreign exchange dealers said they would closely watch overseas trading overnight for any further gains by the dollar against the Japanese currency.
